status: Specified before any patient-level expression/outcome contrasts; cohort outcome counts already known. No response-associated RNA statistics calculated at plan creation.
question: Within the vactosertib+pembrolizumab CRC cohort, are archival screening-linked TGF-beta/fibroblast pathway scores associated with durable clinical benefit (primary5versus23), with objective response alone as a secondary sensitivity (2versus26)?
design_limit: Single-arm observational biomarker association; cannot estimate a biomarker-by-treatment interaction, component-specific benefit, causal TGF-beta dependence or a calibrated personal response probability.

pathway_family.selection: One general TGF-beta response set, one fibroblast TGF-response set, one activated LRRC15CAF state and one cancer-associated ECM programme. Exact gene memberships are fixed before looking at pathway/outcome differences; overlaps are disclosed.
caveats: No bespoke high-result subset will replace a published signature.
Pan-F-TBRS19 exact membership was corroborated in a primary author patent and later publication; original NatureTableS8 download was unavailable.
Pan19 contains contractile genes and is vulnerable to smooth-muscle admixture.
CAF11 andECM-up scores mix cell abundance and per-cell state; biological labels do not establish receptor signalling.
The four sets are correlated; BH controls the defined family under its usual dependence assumptions, not across arbitrary unreported analyses.

data_requirements: Gene-by-sample nonnegative RNA abundance/count matrix or consistently quantified public reads; gene identifiers and units explicit.
Verified sample-to-subject/timepoint linkage and original clinical response labels, never inferred from dose or RNA.
A separate audit must reconcile the28 public subjects versus34(5benefit/29nonbenefit) mentioned in transparent peer review.

normalization_scoring.primary: For each sample, rank all fixed eligible genes by abundance using average ranks for ties; convert to percentile rank100*(rank-0.5)/G. Pathway score is the arithmetic mean of member-gene ranks. The gene universe is fixed across samples before outcome comparisons. All-zero genes across allbaseline samples are removed from universe; a measured zero in an individual sample is retained as zero, not treated as missing.
normalization_scoring.coverage: At least80% of the full published members and at least5genes required; missing genes listed. Same surviving membership used for every sample. Missing genes are not imputed as biological zero.
normalization_scoring.identifier_policy: Gene symbols canonicalized using documented CTGF->CCN2,FAM101B->RFLNB,CYR61->CCN1 aliases; ambiguous duplicate rows are rejected until provenance-resolved.
normalization_scoring.sensitivity: Mean log2(TPM+1) whenTPM available, ormeanlog2(CPM+1) forcounts; and stricter fixed universe>=1TPM/CPM in>=20%ofbaseline samples. Both are sensitivity results, not opportunities to choose the smallerP.
normalization_scoring.comparison_limit: Within-cohort pathway scoring only. Do not insert the patient Caris/Tempus into the trial matrix or call a cross-platform score a calibrated percentile.
normalization_scoring.gene_universe: Prefer fixed GENCODE37 protein-coding gene universe matching the quantified reference; all baseline samples use identical identifiers. Remove only genes zero in everybaseline sample. Save exact measured/retained genes and annotation hashes. If annotation unavailable, stop and resolve rather than silently change universe.
normalization_scoring.original_scoring_boundary: Published gene memberships are used with a new uniform unweighted mean-rank score. This is not an exact reimplementation of each original paper's score (e.g. Dominguez used eigenWeightedMean/PCA weighting), nor a previously validated treatment-selection assay.
